## 2. Regime assessment across three timeframes

**Long-term trend: intact, but maturing.**
- 200-day SMA = **241.108**, rising every session in the visible window (233.0 on 2026-07-02 → 241.11 on 2026-09-30).
- Price is **+3.34%** above it. 50-SMA (256.119) sits **6.2%** above the 200-SMA — the bullish 50>200 alignment has held for the entire Jul 2–Sep 30 window, though the spread has compressed from 9.6% (22.44 points on 2026-07-02) to 6.2% (15.01 points today). That is a trend *maturing*, not reversing.

**Intermediate trend: broken, now rolling over.**
- AMZN closed at its cycle high **284.02 on 2026-08-03** (intraday 287.20) and has not reclaimed it. From that close to 249.15 today = **−12.28%**; peak-to-intraday-trough (287.20 → 244.30 on 2026-09-16) = **−14.94%**.
- Price has been **below the 50-SMA since 2026-09-23**, and has only closed above it twice in the last 14 sessions (2026-09-11 at 256.78 vs 255.25; 2026-09-21 at 258.45 vs 256.10). Repeated failures make the 50-SMA a **ceiling**, not a floor.
- The 50-SMA itself has stopped rising: 256.291 (2026-09-23) → **256.119** (2026-09-30). First four-session decline after a two-month climb from 246.384 (2026-07-30). This is the single most important nuance in the report: **the intermediate trend has stopped supporting price.**

**Short-term: compression / coil.**
- 10-EMA = **249.982**, price 249.15 — essentially pinned to it. The 10-EMA has fallen from 267.16 (2026-08-11) to 249.98, but its daily decline has decelerated sharply: −0.70, −0.52, −1.07, −0.78, **−0.18** over the last five sessions (Sep 23→30). Flattening short-term momentum = base-building, not freefall.
- Structure since the 2026-08-03 top is a **converging wedge**: lower highs (287.20 → 282.79 → 280.14 → 267.56 → 259.49 on 2026-09-21) against **flat-to-higher lows** (244.30 on 2026-09-16 → 244.73 on 2026-09-28 → 246.08 on 2026-09-30).

**Verdict: a corrective consolidation inside a primary uptrend, currently in a low-volatility coil that must resolve directionally within roughly 2–4 weeks.**

---

## 3. Indicator evidence

### Momentum is bearish but decelerating
| Reading | Value | Interpretation |
|---|---|---|
| MACD | **−2.496** | Below zero since **2026-09-09** (first negative print −0.421); 15 consecutive negative sessions |
| MACD signal | **−2.022** | MACD has been below signal since **2026-08-17** (histogram first turned negative at −0.310) |
| Histogram | **−0.474** | Improving from −0.657 (09-29) and −0.614 (09-28) |

The histogram's path is the key tell: it bottomed at **−1.683 on 2026-08-27**, made a *higher* low at **−1.539 on 2026-09-16**, rallied to near zero (**−0.057 on 2026-09-22**), and has rolled back only to −0.474. Price made a **lower low** on 2026-09-16 (244.30) than on 2026-08-27 (255.02) while the histogram made a **higher low** — a mild positive momentum divergence. It is not confirmation; it needs the MACD/signal cross that a close above ~252–253 would likely produce.

### RSI: orderly correction, no capitulation
- RSI = **45.20**. Over the 60-session window RSI has ranged **39.45 (2026-09-16) to 72.23 (2026-08-03)** and has **never printed below 30** during the entire 12% drawdown. That is the signature of *correction*, not *distribution/capitulation*.
- RSI has posted successive higher lows: 39.45 (09-16) → 41.24 (09-28) → 41.93 (09-29) → **45.20**. But it has failed at the mid-line twice (55.85 on 08-28, 52.69 on 09-21), so **RSI 50–53 is the tactical resistance band**; a decisive RSI push through 53 would confirm the momentum turn.

### Volatility: a textbook squeeze
- Bollinger upper **260.814**, middle **252.349**, lower **243.883**.
- Bandwidth = **6.71%** of the mid-band. On **2026-08-19** the same measure was **29.58%** (bands 296.99/220.47). A **77% contraction in six weeks**.
- %B = **31.1%** — price sits in the lower third of the envelope, i.e., weak but not oversold.
- ATR = **5.654**, or **2.27%** of price, versus **9.948 / 3.50%** on 2026-08-03 — a **43% collapse in realized range**.

Tight bands plus collapsing ATR is a coil, not a trend. Squeezes resolve in the direction of the *dominant* trend more often than not, but they are direction-agnostic signals — the breakout level, not the coil itself, is the trade.

### Volume: supply drying up, one buyer response
- **VWMA = 251.161**, and price (249.15) is **0.81% below it**. The volume-weighted average cost of recent positioning sits *above* spot — recent buyers are slightly underwater, which caps rallies into 251–252. VWMA has declined monotonically from 272.05 (2026-08-20), confirming distribution through August.
- The September tape is light: most sessions 24–44M shares versus **129.1M on 2026-07-31** and **90.8M on 2026-08-03**. Declining volume into falling price argues the seller is *exhausting*, not accelerating.
- Today's 41.9M is above the prior two sessions (33.7M, 32.6M) on a +1.01% day — mildly constructive, but the close gave back **1.3% from the 252.44 high**, and 09-30 is a quarter-end session, so treat the volume with some skepticism.

O 246.79 / H 252.44 / L 246.08 / C 249.15. The high **252.44 pierced the 20-SMA at 252.349 by $0.09 and was rejected**, with the close at only 48% of the day's range. That is a precise, mechanical test-and-fail at the first resistance — it tells you exactly where the bulls ran out of bid.

**Gap context (important):** AMZN gapped from a 2026-07-30 close of 235.50 to a 2026-07-31 open of 265.00 (high 273.23, close 271.58) on 129.1M shares, then extended to 287.20 by 2026-08-03. That **239.82–262.01 gap is still unfilled**, and today's 249.15 sits *inside* it. The entire September decline is, structurally, a partial gap-fill retracement. The gap floor (239.82) sits directly beneath the 200-SMA (241.11) and the 50% retracement (241.60) — a triple-confluence demand zone that defines the line between "healthy pullback" and "failed breakout."

---

## 5. Scenarios and execution

**Base case — coil resolves upward (bullish, but trigger-dependent).**
Needs a **daily close above 252.44** on volume ≥ ~40M, then confirmation above **256.12** (50-SMA). Targets: **259.49–260.81**, then **267.56** (2026-08-28 high). A 50-SMA reclaim would also likely flip MACD through its signal line, giving the momentum confirmation that is missing today. Note the coil apex (converging wedge plus descending 20-SMA) lands in roughly the **first half of October**, so this is a near-term decision point, not a Q4 thesis.

**Bear case — support gives way.**
A close below **244.30** opens **243.88** (lower band), then the **239.82–241.60** confluence. If that zone fails on expanding volume/ATR, the post-2026-07-31 structure is invalidated and 235.50 becomes the reference. Watch the 200-SMA: it has not been breached on a closing basis in the visible data, so a close below 241.11 would be a genuine regime change.

**Higher-probability neutral: range trade 244–252.** With ATR at 5.65, a 244–252 band is only ~1.4 ATR wide — too tight for a high-quality swing trade in the middle. Fade only at the edges, or wait for the break.

**Risk parameters (ATR-based, ATR = 5.654):**
- 1×ATR = 5.65 pts (2.27%); 1.5×ATR = 8.48; 2×ATR = 11.31.
- Long from the 246–247 lows with a structural stop below **240.50** (under the 200-SMA and gap floor) risks ~5.5–6.5 pts for a 258–260 target — roughly **2.2:1 to 2.5:1** reward-to-risk.
- A "tight" stop at 243.88 from 249.15 is only ~1 ATR away and sits inside daily noise; it will be shaken out. Size the position off the structural stop, not the band.
- For breakout entries above 252.44, a 1.5×ATR stop (~8.5 pts) is appropriate given that squeezes produce whipsaw.

**Event risk:** this series contains two single-session gaps of **179.2M shares (2026-02-06)** and **129.1M shares (2026-07-31)** that dwarf normal volume. A catalyst of that magnitude can resolve the coil in one session in either direction and will invalidate any stop placed inside the 239.8–260.8 band. Reduce size ahead of any known catalyst rather than after.

---

## 6. What would change the view

| To turn **bullish** | To turn **bearish** |
|---|---|
| Close > 252.44, ideally > 256.12 on >40M shares | Close < 244.30, then < 243.88 |
| RSI > 53 (clears the 50–53 failed-rebound zone) | RSI < 40 again with price at new lows |
| MACD histogram > 0 and MACD > signal | MACD histogram makes a **lower** low below −1.68 |
| Price reclaims VWMA 251.16 and holds | Price loses 200-SMA 241.11 on a closing basis |
| 50-SMA stops falling / price closes above it | 50-SMA crosses down through 20-SMA and keeps falling |

---

## 7. Bottom line

AMZN is **not broken, but it is not working**. The primary uptrend is intact (price +3.3% above a rising 200-SMA; 50>200), yet the intermediate trend has clearly stalled — 12.3% off the 2026-08-03 close, below a now-rolling-over 50-SMA, below VWMA, with MACD negative since 2026-09-09. Simultaneously, volatility has collapsed (bandwidth 6.71% from 29.58%, ATR 2.27% from 3.50%), RSI has bottomed at 39.45 without breaking 30, and the histogram is making higher lows while price made a lower low. That combination — decelerating downside momentum plus an extreme squeeze — favors **patience over prediction**: let the 252.44 / 244.30 boundaries declare themselves. The asymmetry is modestly better to the upside given the primary trend and the 239.8–241.6 confluence beneath, but the honest read is a **neutral coil with a bullish tilt only above 252.44 and a genuine failure below 244.30**.

Items printed with a `2026-09-30` UTC timestamp (e.g. 01:14Z, 03:32Z) fall on **September 29 in New York** because EDT is UTC−4, so they are in-window — but the practical implication is unavoidable:

- All 20 items are **vendor headlines/summaries, not full articles**. No full-text verification of any claim is possible.
- Only **two** supplied items name Amazon in the headline; the rest are peer, sector or thematic pieces where AMZN appears incidentally or not at all.

So this is a **very thin, single-session, late-day sample**, not a representative week of AMZN newsflow. Conclusions below are necessarily low-conviction.

---

## 2. AMZN-specific items (direct)

### 2.1 Amazon reportedly the mystery tenant at Galleria North Tower I, Dallas
**2026-09-29 17:10 ET (21:10Z) · Yahoo ·** https://finnhub.io/api/news?id=89d2d6b2df2b415e17578f277e7d0b8a9cbeec5c2b59df65ca632eb6b490f6a7

The report says the 16-story Galleria North Tower I at 13737 Noel Road will undergo an estimated **$57M two-phase renovation**, per a Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation filing; the tenant is listed as "DFW 22," and the article infers Amazon from the filing's ownership/contact trail.

- **Evidence grade:** headline + summary only; the Amazon identification is explicitly framed as an inference ("appears to be"), not confirmed by Amazon.
- **Impact:** negligible to marginally negative on a standalone basis — a $57M office fit-out is immaterial against Amazon's capex base and adds to the "return-to-office / office footprint" cost line rather than revenue. If anything it is a faint signal of continued Dallas-area corporate expansion.
- **Horizon:** none for the stock; days at most for local real-estate coverage.

### 2.2 Bezos ownership explainer
**2026-09-29 21:14 ET (2026-09-30 01:14Z) · Yahoo ·** https://finnhub.io/api/news?id=b15658a6d7bfa042104d8fc318aa24b516293f4e8b25228e7335eec2bbafdf24

Summary states Bezos' AMZN stake is worth **more than $219 billion as of September 2026**, and that his ownership "has changed dramatically over the past three decades."

- **Evidence grade:** headline + summary; educational/evergreen content, no new filing, no disclosed transaction.
- **Impact:** **neutral**. No supply/demand implication unless an actual sale is disclosed, and none is in the evidence. Worth flagging only as a reminder that a large founder block remains an overhang variable — but that is inference, not news here.

---

## 3. Indirect / thematic items with plausible AMZN read-across

### 3.1 Amazon cited as the weakest big-tech free-cash-flow converter
**2026-09-29 15:20 ET (19:20Z) · Yahoo ·** https://finnhub.io/api/news?id=a7967c24b06427f73d01cc10288db31526e618c49311614800fc516f583dc0bb

The Alphabet piece asserts Alphabet converts ~42¢ of each sales dollar into operating cash but leaves only ~12¢ as free cash flow — "less than any of its big-tech peers **except Amazon**." (In other words, the author places AMZN's FCF conversion below Alphabet's ~12¢.)

- **This is the single most valuation-relevant AMZN datapoint in the sample**, and it is a *negative* framing: heavy AI capital spending compressing FCF.
- **Caveats:** it is an assertion inside a Google-focused article, with no AMZN figures, period definitions, or sourcing given; it is a relative, not absolute, claim; and the market in this window appears to be rewarding AI capex (see 3.4/3.5), so a low FCF conversion is not automatically a negative price driver.
- **Horizon:** weeks to quarters — this feeds the ongoing "is the AI capex cycle worth it" debate rather than a single session.

### 3.2 Data-center buildout skepticism: "$9 trillion may never be built"
**2026-09-29 14:57 ET (18:57Z) · Yahoo ·** https://finnhub.io/api/news?id=26003f223a8c78f017d35d4b9b68f4774d5d99017ec68c74b3965a8a211e3274

A Columbia Business School professor's model suggests **nearly half of planned U.S. data-center capacity may never come online**.

- **Read-across (inference, not stated in the evidence):** two-sided for AMZN. Bearish if AWS's growth/backlog thesis is priced off uninterrupted industry-wide capacity expansion; potentially *supportive* of FCF if it implies the industry (Amazon included) will trim or defer capex, easing the FCF compression flagged in 3.1.
- **Impact:** ambiguous, low-to-moderate magnitude; mostly a sentiment/narrative input.
- **Horizon:** months.

### 3.3 Anthropic cuts AI costs
**2026-09-29 15:12 ET (19:12Z) · Yahoo ·** https://finnhub.io/api/news?id=339f2e58aee2a86eb988d25d67d64f4d88abcdb9d2b48e2c2e06015289665f59

"Better efficiency could reshape the economics of enterprise AI." Headline and summary carry **no mention of Amazon** and no figures.

- **Impact on AMZN: indeterminate.** Cheaper inference is directionally good for AI *adoption* volumes but potentially deflationary for per-unit cloud compute revenue. The evidence does not establish any Amazon linkage, so I will not assert one.
- **Horizon:** quarters; not a tradeable item from this evidence.

A bridge round in lieu of an IPO, which the CEO has delayed over AI-safety concerns.

- **Read-across:** a fresh mega-round is a *positive* signal for aggregate AI infrastructure demand and therefore for hyperscale cloud providers generally, AMZN included. But no Amazon-specific contract, customer or capacity commitment is cited.
- **Impact:** marginal positive for sector sentiment; effectively zero for AMZN idiosyncratically.

**2026-09-29 15:19 ET (19:19Z) · Yahoo ·** https://finnhub.io/api/news?id=81753abf08510cb607b0440483dfb9e964feb80c5a8c24c4ad358cf2e2f03532

- Purely a comparative market-cap observation; **no fundamental AMZN information**. Neutral; at most a mild "mega-cap leadership rotation" narrative item. Horizon: none.

### 3.7 Amazon named among tech giants entering Uzbekistan
**2026-09-29 23:32 ET (2026-09-30 03:32Z) · Yahoo ·** https://finnhub.io/api/news?id=8f44ad2481318fcbb801eafbb686fab4365625fed11cb431675ad655d45e20b9

ICTWeek Uzbekistan 2026 drew 30,000+ visitors and 3,000+ international guests; Amazon is listed among the giants "entering the Uzbek digital market."

- **Impact:** immaterial to AMZN financials; at most a marginal positive for international/emerging-market cloud expansion narrative. The claim is a conference-roundup assertion with no Amazon commitment, investment figure or contract attached. Neutral.

---

## 4. Conflicting evidence

1. **AI capex: boom vs bust within the same afternoon.** OpenAI's $30B raise at ~$1.4T and Anthropic's reported multi-hundred-billion infrastructure expansion (see the SPCX/Anthropic item, 2026-09-29 14:12 ET, https://finnhub.io/api/news?id=f22d2536afa1b0fd11f62e31374251bbbd0624c72f53eb211e9ed596908c47f2) point to *accelerating* demand, while the Columbia model says ~half of planned U.S. data-center capacity may never be built, and Anthropic is simultaneously cutting AI costs. These cannot all be right at the same magnitude; the resolution determines whether AWS's capex is pre-revenue investment or overbuild.
2. **Is low FCF conversion bad or good?** The Google piece frames Amazon's FCF conversion as the weakest among big-tech peers (negative), while the capex-skepticism piece implies capex discipline could *improve* FCF (positive). Same underlying variable, opposite sign depending on whether the market is paying for growth or for cash returns.
3. **Sentiment vs fundamentals.** The tape was described as firm for tech late Tuesday, and SpaceX's market-cap milestone recycles the "mega-cap rotation" theme — both price-action items that carry no AMZN fundamental content and can mask the absence of real catalysts.

---

**Base case: no material AMZN-specific catalyst in the supplied window; expected net impact neutral, with a slight negative tilt from the FCF-conversion framing.**

- **Intraday / 1–3 sessions (Sept 30):** essentially flat, dominated by the broad tech tape. Nothing in this sample is capable of moving a ~$2T-cap name by more than a fraction of a percent on fundamentals. Residual risk is non-news flow (positioning, concentration unwinds).
- **1–4 weeks:** the FCF/capex debate (3.1, 3.2) is the live thread; watch for confirmation or contradiction in actual AMZN disclosures, which this sample does not contain.
- **1–2 quarters:** AI infrastructure demand signals (3.3, 3.4) versus data-center buildout skepticism (3.2) set the range for AWS-related sentiment.

**Confidence: low.** Two direct AMZN items are both immaterial (a $57M office renovation inference and an evergreen ownership explainer); the most valuation-relevant item is a single comparative clause in a competitor's article. 143 of 163 eligible records are absent, and six of the seven calendar days in the window have no supplied coverage at all. ## 9. Actionable insights for traders

**1. Trade the core, not the headline.** Build models on ~**$1.95 core EPS** for Q2-26 and ~**$3.64 for H1-26** (annualised run-rate ~$7.8, before seasonality). Reported GAAP EPS ($5.75 Q2, $8.53 H1, $135.3B TTM net income) embeds ~$3.80/share of non-cash marks in Q2 alone. If the market is anchoring on GAAP EPS, AMZN's multiple looks far cheaper than economic reality — and a mark-down quarter would look like a "miss" even if operations beat.

**2. The Q3 2026 print (late Oct 2026) is a three-variable event.** Watch: (a) revenue ≥ ~$205–210B to sustain the +19% trajectory; (b) operating margin holding ≥13% *despite* D&A +30%+; (c) capex guidance — Q2 alone was $54.2B, TTM $173.0B, and the trend is up. A revenue beat paired with an FCF/capex miss is the most likely negative surprise configuration.

**3. Free cash flow is the pressure point.** TTM FCF is negative and capex intensity has jumped from ~18% to ~26% of revenue. Traders using FCF yield or DCF will get a much lower value than EPS-multiple users. The bull case requires AWS/AI revenue to inflect hard enough in 2027 to justify the depreciation that is already contracted. Position sizing should reflect that this is a 12–24 month thesis, not a 2-quarter one.

**4. Debt is now a rate-sensitive variable.** $82B issued in twelve months, interest expense doubled to a ~$5B+ annualised run-rate. Further issuance is likely while capex runs at $200B+/yr. Rising long yields are now a **direct** earnings and duration headwind for AMZN in a way they were not in 2023–2025.
